text: You wake up choking on your own stomach acid. Can that kill you?
When you lie flat gravity stops holding the acid down in your stomach.
A ring of muscle at the top of your stomach is supposed to stay shut.
After a big late meal it can slip open and acid creeps up your throat.
If it touches your voice box the cords slam shut and you wake up gasping.
It's scary but it usually lets go in a few seconds.
The bigger risk is acid slipping into your lungs. That can cause pneumonia.
And years of burns can damage your throat and raise your cancer risk.
So can it kill you in your sleep? It's very rare.
Raise the head of your bed about six inches.
And stop eating three hours before bed.
If it happens most nights see a doctor.
